system: FKBP12 with three low affinity ligands
protocol: WExplore (first application to ligand release)
outcome: Ligand residence times and exit pathways from unbiased WE unbinding ensembles, WExplore more efficient than conventional MD even for ns scale unbinding, numbers not verified (full text not accessible)

system: Trypsin and benzamidine (PDB 3PTB)
protocol: WExplore (5 runs of 48 walkers), CHARMM with OpenMM 6.3, CGenFF ligand
outcome: Unbinding MFPT 180 μs from 4.1 μs of total sampling versus experimental 1700 μs (within an order of magnitude), multiple exit pathways

system: T4 lysozyme L99A with benzene (PDB 1L83), benzene exit from the buried cavity, CHARMM36 with GB implicit solvent
protocol: WESTPA with Voronoi bins (23 to 26 centers per pathway), 4 to 5 walkers per bin, τ 2 ps at 300 K or 10 ps at 400 K, GROMACS 4.5, about 29 µs aggregate
outcome: Four benzene exit pathways found, preliminary per pathway rates (values only in a figure, not verified) with two pathways close to the experimental k_off of 950 per s at 303 K and two faster

system: Soluble epoxide hydrolase with inhibitor TPPU
protocol: WExplore, engine not verified
outcome: Residence time 42 s (standard error range 23 to 280 s) from 6 μs of sampling and 75 unbinding events, versus experimental 11 min (660 s)

system: Baz2B bromodomain with ICR7 (PDB 4XUB)
protocol: WExplore (3 runs of 48 walkers per pose, two docked poses), CHARMM with OpenMM interface, CHARMM36 and CGenFF
outcome: Pose A k_off 2.4 × 10⁶ s⁻¹ (MFPT 420 ns) versus pose B 6.6 × 10⁶ s⁻¹ (150 ns), exit rate ranking agrees with the crystal pose, 8.4 μs total over both bromodomains

system: Brd4 first bromodomain with MS436 (PDB 4NUD)
protocol: WExplore (3 runs of 48 walkers per pose, two docked poses), CHARMM with OpenMM interface, CHARMM36 and CGenFF
outcome: Pose A k_off 3.6 s⁻¹ (MFPT 280 ms) versus pose B 2.2 × 10³ s⁻¹ (0.46 ms), about 600 fold slower exit from pose A, ranking agrees with the crystal pose, 81% of transitions between deeply bound states pass through the unbound state (both systems)

system: Trypsin and benzamidine (PDB 3PTB)
protocol: REVO (regionless WE, introduced here) compared with WExplore, wepy with OpenMM 7.2.2
outcome: Residence time 3.76 ms with REVO (WExplore 1.19, unit not printed) versus experimental 1.6 ms, from 8.75 μs per method, and a new fourth exit pathway

system: BPTF bromodomain with inhibitor (S) 1, the active AU1 enantiomer
protocol: WExplore from multiple docked poses with a weighted network model of poses, engine not verified
outcome: Predicted pose ensemble places the methyl ester as an acetyl lysine mimic hydrogen bonded to conserved N2881, aryl stacking on F2887 and urea bonded to D2834, consistent with SAR (racemate K_d 2.8 μM), no rate reported

system: T4 lysozyme L99A with p xylene (OBC GBSA implicit solvent)
protocol: wepy (introduced here) with REVO and WExplore resamplers, OpenMM, Amber ff96 and GAFF
outcome: Over 4 × 1 μs per group REVO gave 4337 and WExplore 486 unbinding events versus 39 for unresampled ensembles, all WE replicates exited within 100 ns versus about 300 ns for the first straightforward exit, straightforward reference rate 3.25 μs⁻¹

system: Soluble epoxide hydrolase catalytic domain (PDB 4OD0) with TPPU analog ligand 1
protocol: REVO with wepy and OpenMM, CHARMM36 (48 walkers), WE MSM
outcome: WE MSM residence time 3.1 min (best model) versus experimental 14.25 min, 34 unbinding events in 14.72 μs

system: HIF 2α PAS B domain and THS 017 ligand escaping a buried cavity (PDB 3H7W), ff19SB and GAFF2
protocol: Steady state WE, three stage MAB, 3D coordinate (cavity SASA, unbinding RMSD, ligand receptor distance), τ 100 ps, 8 walkers per bin, WESS reweighting, three runs, WESTPA 2.0 on 16 A100 GPUs
outcome: k_off 1.3 × 10^4 to 8.7 × 10^4 s−1 against ZZ exchange NMR 1.4 ± 0.3 s−1 (MFPT 0.71 s), so far too fast. More than 4000 pathways from 35.1 to 41.5 μs per run in 14 to 16 days, two exit routes (63% and 37%), gating residue N288 confirmed by NMR on N288A and N288Q

system: Kinesin Eg5 motor domain and ADP (PDB 1II6), ADP release, explicit water, 100 mM NaCl
protocol: MABL (minimal adaptive binless WE) against multi MAB, progress score from ligand receptor interaction energy, unbinding RMSD and distance, τ 50 ps, WESTPA 2.0 with Amber 22 pmemd.cuda and ff19SB
outcome: First unbinding event after 2.0 μs aggregate with MABL against 4.7 μs with multi MAB, more than 50% more efficient, 43.8 μs over 44 protocols. No rate constant estimated (seconds timescale process)

system: Soluble epoxide hydrolase (PDB 4OD0) with an isobutyrylpiperidinyl trifluoromethoxyphenyl urea TPPU analog
protocol: Merging bias corrected MSMs (MBC MSM, introduced here) built on REVO wepy unbinding data (17.03 μs, reused from Bose 2023)
outcome: Long lag MBC MSM median MFPT about 50 min and standard MSM at τ = τ_WE median 0.96 min, direct WE flux 3.5 min, versus experimental 27.1 min

system: HIF 2α PAS B and THS 017 unbinding, existing ensemble of 4177 WE pathways from Silvestrini 2024
protocol: Reanalysis only, three stage MAB WE runs from Silvestrini 2024 (WESTPA 2.0, 35.1 to 41.5 μs per run), pathways clustered with PRISM in MDANCE
outcome: PRISM split the two exit routes 53.4% and 46.6% (SHINE 52.0% and 48.0%). No new simulation
reference: Woody Santos, 2026, Digital Discovery, volume and page not verified, 10.1039/D6DD00288A

system: Hepatitis B virus capsid assembly from dimeric subunits (PDB 1QGT), rigid α carbon Go model with energy tables, 120 dimer capsid with 300 dimers in total
protocol: WESTPA 1.0.0 beta driving tabulated Monte Carlo, 2D progress coordinate (dimers in the largest partial capsid, distance of the nearest free dimer to an empty site), 16 or 4 walkers per bin
outcome: WE produced pathways for the final about 25 percent of assembly, reaching a complete 120 dimer capsid from a 110 dimer start (113 to 117 dimers from a 90 dimer start), tabulation sped up Monte Carlo by up to 6700 times

system: Barnase and barstar (wild type, R59A, uncharged isosteres), PDB 1BRS
protocol: Steady state WE in the NAM framework, WESTPA with UIOWA_BD Brownian dynamics, coarse grained
outcome: Basal k_on (2.85 ± 1.30) × 10⁶ M⁻¹ s⁻¹ with HI, R59A k_on agrees with experiment, WE 6 to 131 fold more efficient than brute force

system: MDM2 (25 to 109) and p53 peptide (17 to 29)
protocol: WE with fixed bins on 2D RMSD, WESTPA, ff99SB ILDN with GB/SA
outcome: k_on (7 ± 4) × 10⁷ M⁻¹ s⁻¹ against experiment 9.2 × 10⁶ (8 fold), 182 binding pathways, about 6 fold more efficient than brute force

system: MDM2 and p53 peptide with four preorganization analogues, PDB 1YCR
protocol: Steady state WE in the NAM framework, WESTPA with UIOWA_BD, Cα Gō models with HI
outcome: k_on (5.7 ± 0.6) × 10⁷ M⁻¹ s⁻¹ disordered against (5.1 ± 0.8) × 10⁷ preorganized, within error

system: Barnase and barstar, PDB 1BRS
protocol: Equilibrium WE on a 2D coordinate, WESTPA with GROMACS 4.6.7, ff03* and TIP3P explicit solvent
outcome: k_on (2.3 ± 1.0) × 10⁸ M⁻¹ s⁻¹ against experiment (2.86 ± 0.7) × 10⁸, 203 binding pathways from 18 μs aggregate

system: Barnase and barstar association (PDB 1BRS), explicit TIP3P water, about 100 000 atoms
protocol: RED scheme applied to the single equilibrium WE run of Saglam 2019 (650 iterations, τ 20 ps, 1600 walkers, 18 μs), GROMACS 4.6.7 with ff03*
outcome: RED at least 25% more effective than the original estimate, most probable event duration 6 ns, k_on compared with experiment in Fig. 4. Numeric k_on not verified

system: Barnase and barstar association
protocol: RED analysis through the new w_red tool applied to the earlier atomistic WE run, WESTPA 2.0
outcome: RED more than 25% more efficient than the original WE estimate of k_on (Fig. 7B, same data as DeGrave 2021). Numeric k_on not verified

system: SMARCA2 bromodomain, VHL and degrader PROTAC 2 ternary complex (PDB 6HAX)
protocol: WE HDX, REVO (OpenMM 7.5.0) and binned WE (WESTPA) along HDX MS derived contact collective variables
outcome: Minimum interface RMSD reached 2.5 Å within 0.5 μs of aggregate WE versus 10 Å after 1.4 μs of conventional MD, 3278 uniquely bound ternary complexes in 6 of 7 runs, predicted binding rate significantly slower than the other degraders (no experimental value)

system: AM2 receptor (CLR and RAMP3, membrane embedded) with adrenomedullin 2/intermedin peptide (rebuilt cryo EM PDB 6UVA)
protocol: REVO with wepy and OpenMM, CHARMM36 (3 × 48 walkers, 5.76 μs per system), G protein mimicked by restraints
outcome: AM2/IMD hinge hydrogen bonds (R33 to D90, R23 to D96 salt bridge) held with higher probability and lower CLR ECD loop RMSD than AM, a more stable bound complex consistent with the measured slower off rate, kinetic numbers not given for simulations

system: HIV 1 capsid protein C terminal domain dimer (CA CTD, reference NMR PDB 2KOD), explicit water, pH 6.5
protocol: WE with fixed bins on heavy atom RMSD (0.5 Å spacing from 0 to 8 Å), τ 100 ps, 4 walkers per bin, 200 iterations, WESTPA, data plotted with WEDAP
outcome: Plotting showcase only, 0.8 μs of WE and a 1 μs standard MD run, no kinetic number reported

system: HIV 1 capsid protein C terminal domain dimer interconversion, discrete state synthetic MD (SynD) from an MSM built on about 90 μs of standard MD, 100 ps lag
protocol: Reinforcement learning WE (WE RL) that reweights four candidate coordinates (two orientation angles, T188 to T188 distance, C2 angle) during the run, against least counts binless WE and binned WE (10 bins on T188 distance, 8 walkers per bin), 80 walkers, five runs of 2000 iterations, WESTPA 2.0
outcome: MSM reference MFPT 3.83 μs. WE RL sampled transitions slightly faster than binned WE but needed marginally more time to converge the rate, T188 distance learned as the key coordinate, about 0.24 ms of synthetic time. Numeric rates and gains only in figures, not verified. Preprint
reference: Yang, 2024, bioRxiv preprint, no volume or page, 10.1101/2024.10.09.617475

system: HIV 1 capsid protein C terminal domain dimer (CA CTD), interconversion of the major D1 dimer (NMR PDB 2KOD) and hidden D2 dimer, AMBER ff15ipq
protocol: Equilibrium WE then steady state WE (three runs per direction) with MAB (25 to 30 bins, 4 walkers per bin) on helix orientation angles, MSM on WE seeded MD, WESTPA 2.0 with AMBER 22 pmemd on A100 GPUs, 120 μs of WE in all
outcome: D1 to D2 (k12) and D2 to D1 (k21) rates from steady state WE within the same order of magnitude as 19F EXSY NMR, with k12 slower than k21 as in experiment, while MSM rates were about tenfold too fast. Numeric rates only in Fig. 5 and Table S1, not verified

system: 4 fluoro W184 labeled HIV 1 CA CTD dimer, D1 and D2 interconversion, ff15ipq fluorinated aromatic parameters
protocol: Independent replicate conventional MD, equilibrium WE and steady state WE, same MAB protocol, WESTPA 2.0 with AMBER 22
outcome: Steady state WE rates close to the 19F NMR values measured on this same labeled construct. Numeric rates not verified

system: DCAF15 and RBM39 with molecular glue E7820 (PDB 6PAI)
protocol: REVO with wepy and OpenMM 8.0 on a weakened interface (interprotein nonbonded terms scaled by λ = 0.15), 48 walkers × 500 cycles, 10 replicates
outcome: High potency glue kept stable interface contacts, interface distance at the 10⁻⁸ probability threshold tracks experimental EC50 across the glue series with R² = 0.92

system: CLR and RAMP1 extracellular domain complex with CGRP(27 37) peptide (template PDB 4RWG)
protocol: REVO with wepy and OpenMM, CHARMM36 (12 runs × 48 walkers), WE MSM
outcome: 89 unbinding events, MSM MFPT 7.5 × 10⁻⁶ s versus 0.02 s for ssCGRP(27 37), about 2700 fold slowing versus the 430 fold longer experimental residence time of ssCGRP (numbers from bioRxiv preprint 10.1101/2025.06.13.659569, journal full text not accessible)

system: Calmodulin N terminal domain (residues 4 to 75), apo (PDB 1CFD) to holo (PDB 1CLL) transition, united residue bistable Go model
protocol: WE (Huber and Kim) with 1D DRMSD bins and M = 40 per bin, dynamical Metropolis Monte Carlo, in house code
outcome: k_WE (1.9 ± 0.4) × 10^−10 per MC step against brute force (2.1 ± 0.2) × 10^−10 per MC step at kBT/ε 0.5, efficiency gain about 5, 15 and 100 at kBT/ε 0.5, 0.45 and 0.4
reference: Zhang 2007, Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 104, 18043, doi 10.1073/pnas.0706349104

system: Adenylate kinase (E. coli, 214 residues), open apo (PDB 4AKE) to closed holo (PDB 1AKE), three semiatomistic models with all atom backbone and β carbons
protocol: WE path sampling on a DRMSD progress coordinate, 25 bins with 20 trajectories per bin, library based Monte Carlo dynamics, in house code
outcome: Model 3 closed to open rate 2.5 × 10^−6 per τ, 50 equal weight transitions after resampling in about 2 weeks of one CPU against an estimated 4 years per brute force transition, two distinct pathways found
reference: Bhatt 2010, J Chem Theory Comput 6, 3527, doi 10.1021/ct100406t

system: Chignolin (PDB 1UAO)
protocol: WExplore (hierarchical Voronoi WE, introduced here), CHARMM with CHARMM22/CMAP
outcome: 522 configuration states from folded to fully unfolded found in 96 ns of WExplore sampling, a much smaller set found by a 1.2 μs conventional GPU trajectory, 10.2 μs total WE sampling

system: HIV 1 reverse transcriptase RNase H domain (residues 427 to 556 of PDB 1DLO), wild type and F440A, F440A/T477A mutants
protocol: WE simulations run as a check on 200 ns NAMD MD (WE details only in the SI, not verified)
outcome: WE supported that RNH F440A is less stable than the T477A compensated double mutant and wild type (qualitative, number not verified)

system: WasCFP cyan fluorescent protein variant (built from mCerulean PDB 2WSO)
protocol: WE along a chromophore hydration coordinate (48 walkers, 470 ns), CHARMM with OpenMM 5.2, then CPHMD MSλD
outcome: Transient partially open β barrel state with chromophore pKa 6.8 versus 31.7 for the closed form, population 12% at pH 6.1 rising to 53% at pH 8.1

reference: Suárez 2016, J Chem Theory Comput 12, 3473, doi 10.1021/acs.jctc.6b00339

outcome: History labeled MFPTs matched the long MD reference while history independent Markov MFPTs were shorter by one or more orders of magnitude (per protein values only in figures, not verified)

system: Calbindin AFF Ca²⁺ sensor (113 residues) and mutants
protocol: Equilibrium then steady state WE, WESTPA with Brownian dynamics of a native centric model
outcome: WE pathways predicted Phe to Ala mutations that raised measured switching rates up to 32 fold, negative control L31A changed rates 1.03 and 1.57 fold

system: Chignolin, PDB 1UAO
protocol: Steady state WE with fixed RMSD bins, WESTPA with sander, ff14SBonlysc and GB at 275 K
outcome: Folding and unfolding rates roughly agree with a 4 μs brute force reference (figures only), threefold spread among runs
reference: Bogetti 2019, Living J Comput Mol Sci 1, 10607, 10.33011/livecoms.1.2.10607

system: NTL9 (PDB 2HBB) folding, implicit solvent, 15 WESTPA runs from the Adhikari 2019 study
protocol: Reanalysis of steady state WESTPA folding runs (about 60 µs aggregate) with standard and Bayesian bootstrap, no new simulation
outcome: Arithmetic mean folding rate 5.868 × 10^2 per s with standard error 4.928 × 10^2 per s from 15 values spanning about 20 orders of magnitude, nominal 95 percent intervals of both bootstraps underestimate the true mean in about 30 percent of synthetic tests
reference: Mostofian 2019, J Chem Theory Comput 15, 3499, doi 10.1021/acs.jctc.9b00015

system: Protein G B1 domain (PDB 1PGA) folding, implicit solvent, 13 WESTPA runs from the Adhikari 2019 study
protocol: Reanalysis of steady state WESTPA folding runs (about 200 µs aggregate) with standard and Bayesian bootstrap, no new simulation
outcome: Arithmetic mean folding rate 1.870 × 10^−2 per s with standard error 1.857 × 10^−2 per s from 13 values spanning about 70 orders of magnitude, Bayesian bootstrap preferred when the log10 standard deviation exceeds 1
reference: Mostofian 2019, J Chem Theory Comput 15, 3499, doi 10.1021/acs.jctc.9b00015

system: NTL9 folding, AMBER ff14SB with implicit solvent at low (γ 5 per ps) and water like (γ 80 per ps) friction
protocol: Steady state WE with recycling, WESTPA with GPU AMBER, 10 and 30 independent runs (115 and 252 µs aggregate), direct flux and haMSM (10,000 microstates) with Bayesian bootstrap
outcome: Folding time 0.8 to 9.0 µs (haMSM) at γ 5 per ps and 0.2 to 1.9 ms (haMSM, direct WE 0.01 to 0.80 ms) at γ 80 per ps, experiment about 1 ms, nominal 95 percent credibility regions
reference: Adhikari 2019, J Am Chem Soc 141, 6519, doi 10.1021/jacs.8b10735 (correction 2021, J Am Chem Soc 143, 7588, doi 10.1021/jacs.0c02854)

system: Protein G B1 domain folding, AMBER ff14SB with implicit solvent at low friction (γ 5 per ps)
protocol: Steady state WE with recycling, WESTPA with GPU AMBER, 15 independent runs (225 µs aggregate), direct flux and haMSM with Bayesian bootstrap
outcome: Folding time 3.3 to 200 ms by WE haMSM (direct WE 4 to 210 s), corrected experimental value 2 to 40 ms, obtained with far less than 1 ms of aggregate simulation
reference: Adhikari 2019, J Am Chem Soc 141, 6519, doi 10.1021/jacs.8b10735 (correction 2021, J Am Chem Soc 143, 7588, doi 10.1021/jacs.0c02854)

system: NTL9 folding, implicit solvent atomistic model at water like friction, 30 WE runs harvested from Adhikari 2019
lab: Zuckerman, Aristoff, Makarov and Simpson (OHSU, Colorado State, UT Austin, Drexel)
protocol: Transient current bounds on the steady state current (Smoluchowski theory) applied to existing WE flux profiles, no new simulation
outcome: Flux profile approached steady state monotonically out to 45 ns molecular time (about 225 µs aggregate), Hill relation folding time 0.2 to 2.0 ms consistent with experiment

system: p53 N terminal 15 residue peptide from the MDM2 bound crystal structure (intermediate tutorial)
protocol: WESTPA with a two dimensional progress coordinate, Amber sander, ff14SBonlysc with GB implicit solvent at 275 K
outcome: Conformational sampling tutorial starting from the bound α helix, no quantitative result reported in text (not verified)
reference: Bogetti 2019, Living J Comput Mol Sci 1, 10607, 10.33011/livecoms.1.2.10607

system: Chignolin folding and unfolding (advanced tutorial 1)
protocol: Steady state WE in WESTPA on an RMSD coordinate (4 walkers per bin), Amber, ff14SBonlysc with GB implicit solvent at 275 K
outcome: WE folding and unfolding rate constants roughly agree with brute force MD values of 0.71 × 10⁷ s⁻¹ (folding) and 0.13 × 10⁸ s⁻¹ (unfolding), threefold spread among WE runs equals about 0.6 kcal/mol in barrier
reference: Bogetti 2019, Living J Comput Mol Sci 1, 10607, 10.33011/livecoms.1.2.10607

system: NTL9 folding, implicit solvent atomistic model at low friction (γ 5 per ps)
protocol: haMSM on fine k means microbins (pyEMMA, all atom RMSD, PCA or VAMP features) built from transient 2D WE data (WESTPA protocol of Adhikari 2019), lag equal to WE τ 10 ps
outcome: haMSM gave an order of magnitude steady state flux within 1 ns of molecular time (about 1/5 of the 5 ns relaxation, 3.7 µs aggregate) and a flux inside the validation interval within 2.5 ns (11.8 µs aggregate)
reference: Copperman 2020, J Chem Theory Comput 16, 6763, doi 10.1021/acs.jctc.0c00273

system: Protein G (streptococcal IgG binding domain) folding, implicit solvent atomistic model at low friction (γ 5 per ps)
protocol: haMSM microbins on 15 2D WE runs (225 µs aggregate), then WE restarted twice from the haMSM steady state (rw1 76 µs aggregate)
outcome: haMSM steady state flux about 3 orders of magnitude above the direct flux, restarted WE gave a folding time of 0.3 to 4.3 ms against experimental 3.1 ms (pH 4.0) to 39 ms (pH 11.2)
reference: Copperman 2020, J Chem Theory Comput 16, 6763, doi 10.1021/acs.jctc.0c00273

system: Trp cage folding, 208 µs DESRES atomistic trajectory
protocol: Iterative reweighting of short unbiased trajectory segments for stationary distributions and committors (precursor of RiteWeight), no WE resampling
outcome: Stationary distribution and committor estimates from short segments (numbers not verified, abstract only). Preprint, no journal version found

system: SARS CoV 2 spike head, glycosylated, RBD closed to open, explicit water (stated as about 500 000 atoms, and about 600 000 in another passage)
protocol: WE with τ 100 ps, 8 walkers per bin, 24 basis states, bins adjusted by hand, WESTPA with AMBER 18 on GPUs, WE data later used to train a variational autoencoder
outcome: First run about 7.5 μs in 8.77 days on 80 P100 GPUs, then about 70.0 μs after 1099 iterations in 26.74 days on 100 V100 GPUs. Second independent run about 51.5 μs in 19.64 days with opening and further RBD peeling. No rate constant (Gordon Bell special prize work)
reference: Casalino, 2021, Int J High Perform Comput Appl, 35, 432, 10.1177/10943420211006452

system: Calbindin alternate frame folding Ca2+ sensor switch (E65′Q calbindin AFF construct, N′ to N), residue level Gō type model
protocol: RED scheme against the original steady state flux estimate, ten WE runs reanalyzed from DeGrave 2018 (2D RMSD coordinate, τ 100 ps, 65 μs each), WESTPA with UIOWA BD
outcome: RED reproduced the switching rate of 50 standard 2 μs runs with the first 25% of the WE data, almost 50% more efficient than the original estimate, which underestimated the rate twofold. Rate value itself in Table S1, not verified

system: SARS CoV 2 spike head, residues 16 to 1140, fully glycosylated, RBD down (PDB 6VXX) to up (6VSB) and open, explicit water, almost half a million atoms
protocol: Equilibrium WE, 2D coordinate (spike core to RBD center of mass distance and RBD RMSD), two independent runs, WESTPA 2020.02 with AMBER 18 on 100 GPUs
outcome: More than 130 μs and 310 pathways (204 down to up, 106 down to open), N343 glycan gates opening, N343A cut ACE2 binding by about 56% in biolayer interferometry. No rate constant

system: p53 N terminal peptide, residues 17 to 29 (from PDB 1YCR), GB implicit solvent
protocol: Equilibrium WE with MAB against manual bins, 2D coordinate (RMSD to the MDM2 bound helix and end to end distance), WESTPA with AMBER18
outcome: MAB occupied 66% of its bins (29 of 44) against 17% (50 of 294) for manual bins with 2.0 μs per scheme, and reached a low probability region of left handed helix and PPII conformations missed by manual bins

system: Chignolin, folding and unfolding, DESRES equilibrium MD
lab: Zuckerman, Chodera and Noé (OHSU, MSKCC, FU Berlin)
protocol: haMSM against variationally validated MSMs (PyEMMA), reanalysis of existing MD, no WE resampling
outcome: MSM MFPTs accurate only at lag times of about 100 ns or more, haMSM MFPTs and pathway statistics accurate at the MD frame interval with 1 to 10 ns of history (values only in figures, not verified)
reference: Suárez 2021, J Chem Theory Comput 17, 3119, doi 10.1021/acs.jctc.0c01154

outcome: 85% average reduction in trajectory file size against WESTPA 1.0. Storage test only

system: NTL9 protein folding (millisecond process)
protocol: WE with the haMSM restarting plugin (msm_we) and non Markovian FPT distribution (NonMarkovFPT), WESTPA 2.0 with AMBER 16
outcome: haMSM restarts accelerated convergence of the folding rate constant toward the direct WE flux (Fig. 9B), FPT distribution and MFPT from the final haMSM (Fig. 9C). Numeric rate and MFPT not verified

system: BdpA G29A natural backbone, unfolding and unfolded state at 25 °C (NMR structure from this paper, reference PDB 1BDC)
protocol: Two stage WE (unfolding from the folded NMR structure, then sampling from unfolded conformations), haMSM reweighting to equilibrium populations, WESTPA 2.0 with the ff15ipq protein mimetic force field
outcome: Unfolded state most probable R_g 12.7 Å, unfolded ensembles keep 67 to 80% native contacts across the series but only 2 to 13% between helices. Experimental ΔG° of unfolding 5.2 ± 0.3 kcal/mol (not computed by WE)

system: BdpA β3 H2 variant, four β3 residues in helix 2
protocol: Same two stage WE and haMSM protocol
outcome: Unfolded state R_g 14.5 Å, about 15% more expanded than the natural backbone. Experimental ΔG° 1.9 ± 0.4 kcal/mol

system: BdpA β3 H3 variant, four β3 residues in helix 3
protocol: Same two stage WE and haMSM protocol
outcome: Unfolded state R_g 14.8 Å. Experimental ΔG° 1.1 ± 0.4 kcal/mol

system: BdpA Aib H2 variant, four Aib residues in helix 2
protocol: Same two stage WE and haMSM protocol
outcome: Unfolded state shows an extra compact misfolded population at R_g about 11.5 Å. Experimental ΔG° 3.4 ± 0.2 kcal/mol

system: BdpA Aib H3 variant, four Aib residues in helix 3
protocol: Same two stage WE and haMSM protocol
outcome: Unfolded state R_g distribution and long range contacts closest to the natural backbone, matching its near native experimental ΔG° of 5.1 ± 0.3 kcal/mol

system: p53 peptide conformational sampling
protocol: Tutorial 7.2, 2D progress coordinate with bins adjusted on the fly and auxiliary data tracking, WESTPA 2.0
outcome: Teaching example, no new benchmark number reported
reference: Bogetti, 2023, Living J Comput Mol Sci, 5, 1655, 10.33011/livecoms.5.1.1655

system: Chignolin β hairpin (PDB 1UAO) folding and unfolding, GB implicit solvent, ff14SBonlysc, 275 K
protocol: Tutorial 7.3, steady state WE on Cα RMSD, three runs per direction, WESTPA 2.0 with Amber
outcome: WE unfolding and folding rate constants roughly comparable to a 4 μs brute force run, folding slower to converge. Numeric rates shown only in Figs. 10 and 11, not verified
reference: Bogetti, 2023, Living J Comput Mol Sci, 5, 1655, 10.33011/livecoms.5.1.1655

system: NTL9 protein folding (millisecond process)
protocol: Tutorial 7.7, haMSM restarting plugin (msm_we) with flux and committor analysis, WESTPA 2.0 with Amber 16
outcome: Teaching example, no new rate number verified
reference: Bogetti, 2023, Living J Comput Mol Sci, 5, 1655, 10.33011/livecoms.5.1.1655

system: Human glutathione S transferase A1 1 homodimer (hGSTA1 1), ligand free, from PDB 1K3L with ligand removed
protocol: WE with MAB (5 bins), τ 50 ps, 5 walkers per bin, α9 helix RMSD coordinate, three runs, WESTPA 2.0 on 16 A100 GPUs, validated by Cu(II) EPR distances
outcome: Pathways for the alternate state transition of helix α9 (a seconds timescale process per prior work) from 690 ns in 1.6 days and 309 ns in 16.8 h, showing mutually exclusive α9 docking (negative cooperativity). No rate constant

system: SARS CoV 2 Delta variant spike head (residues 13 to 1140), glycosylated, RBD down to up and open, explicit water
protocol: WE coupled to DeepDriveMD (AI driven progress coordinate stratification), haMSM analysis, WESTPA 2.0 with AMBER20 on 192 V100 GPUs
outcome: More than 800 opening pathways from 72 μs in 14 days, 83 reaching an ACE2 bound like open state and 18 a dramatically open state. First opening (up) after 14 μs in 4 days, coupling claimed to give a 100 fold gain in phase space exploration. Numeric opening rate not verified
reference: Dommer, 2023, Int J High Perform Comput Appl, 37, 28, 10.1177/10943420221128233

system: SARS CoV 2 wild type spike opening, existing WE data
lab: Amaro, Chong, Zuckerman and consortium (UC San Diego led)
protocol: Parallelized, memory optimized haMSM analysis of TB scale WE data, no new WE run reported for this system
outcome: haMSM gave steady state opening rate constants from transient WE data, improving prior estimates by many orders of magnitude (values only in a figure, not verified)
reference: Dommer 2023, Int J High Perform Comput Appl 37, 28, doi 10.1177/10943420221128233

system: BdpA (B domain of staphylococcal protein A) G29A, natural backbone (PDB 7TIO), explicit SPC/Eb water
protocol: Steady state WE folding, MAB with 15 bins, τ 100 ps, 5 walkers per bin, five runs, iterative haMSM reweighting and restart (msm_we), WESTPA 2.0 with AMBER 20 and the ff15ipq protein mimetic force field, 66 μs on 24 V100 GPUs
outcome: k_f (1.1 ± 0.9) × 10^5 s−1 at 25 °C against 8.3 × 10^4 s−1 by temperature jump (F13W, 10 °C)

system: BdpA β3 H2 variant, four α to β3 residue swaps in helix 2 (PDB 7TIP)
protocol: Same WE protocol as the natural backbone, 114 μs aggregate
outcome: k_f (3.4 ± 2.9) × 10^3 s−1 at 25 °C against NMR line shape (0.39 ± 0.13) × 10^3 s−1 at 10 °C (τ_f 2.5 ms)

system: BdpA β3 H3 variant, four α to β3 residue swaps in helix 3 (PDB 7TIR)
protocol: Same WE protocol, 176 μs aggregate

system: BdpA β3/βcyc H2 variant with two cyclic ACPC residues in helix 2 (PDB 7URJ, NMR structure from this paper)
protocol: Same WE protocol, 62 μs aggregate
outcome: k_f (2.1 ± 2.5) × 10^3 s−1 at 25 °C against NMR (1.1 ± 0.1) × 10^3 s−1 at 10 °C (τ_f 900 μs), simulation could not resolve its ranking against β3 H2

system: ARNT PAS B domain, ligand free, opening of the internal water filled cavity
protocol: WE on a 1D coordinate (SASA of cavity lining residues), 600 iterations, WESTPA 2.0 with AMBER 22 and ff19SB, WE pathway conformations used for HADDOCK ensemble docking of KG 655 and KG 279
outcome: 8 μs of WE gave cavity open receptor conformations with cavity SASA 220 to 290 Å², supporting NOE restrained internal binding poses. No rate constant

system: NTL9 folding (PDB 2HBB reference), discrete state synthetic MD from an MSM built on 2.5 μs of GB implicit solvent MD (ff14SB, low viscosity)
protocol: Deep learning enhanced binless WE, convolutional VAE latent space of Cα contact maps retrained on the fly, local outlier factor plus RMSD picks walkers to split, M = 72 walkers, compared with binless RMSD and MAB binned controls
outcome: k_fold 3.0 × 10^5 s−1 (on the fly DL) and 6.7 × 10^5 s−1 (pretrained DL) against an MSM ground truth (value shown only in a figure, not verified). Efficiency S_k 2.2 and 3.0 against the binless control, 1.3 and 1.8 against MAB, so more than 3 fold at best

system: SARS CoV 2 Ancestral (D614) spike, glycosylated, RBD closed to up and open, CHARMM36m and TIP3P
protocol: Equilibrium WE with MAB, 2D coordinate (RBD to core distance and RMSD to PDB 6VSB), 50 starting structures, WESTPA 2020.02 with Amber 18 on 64 to 112 A100 GPUs, pathways clustered with LPATH
outcome: 79 μs over 600 iterations. Mean pathway sampling time closed to up 40.59 ± 3.17 ns and closed to open 45.45 ± 1.69 ns, a relative readiness measure and not a rate. D614 to K854 salt bridge must break before opening
reference: Kearns, 2026, Proc Natl Acad Sci USA, 123, e2504793123, 10.1073/pnas.2504793123

system: SARS CoV 2 Delta spike, glycosylated (no N17 glycan), RBD opening
protocol: Same MAB WE protocol as the Ancestral spike
outcome: 34 μs over 270 iterations. Mean pathway sampling time closed to up 11.68 ± 2.78 ns and closed to open 16.53 ± 2.73 ns, faster than the Ancestral spike. Not a rate
reference: Kearns, 2026, Proc Natl Acad Sci USA, 123, e2504793123, 10.1073/pnas.2504793123

system: SARS CoV 2 Omicron BA.1 spike, glycosylated, RBD opening
protocol: Same MAB WE protocol as the Ancestral spike
outcome: 36 μs over 400 iterations. Mean pathway sampling time closed to up 17.70 ± 6.54 ns and closed to open 20.17 ± 4.55 ns, unique "peel" state beyond super open. Not a rate
reference: Kearns, 2026, Proc Natl Acad Sci USA, 123, e2504793123, 10.1073/pnas.2504793123

system: Human adenylate kinase, unliganded, GB implicit solvent (GBNeck2, ff14SBonlysc), WE seeded from AI generated ensembles (AFsample2 and ESMFlow, 20 to 80 structures each)
protocol: WE on the first two principal components (400 bins, τ 10 ps, 8 walkers per bin, WESTPA, A100 GPUs), then RiteWeight reweighting of WE segments to equilibrium (WE plus RW)
outcome: Differences among the AI seeded ensembles were largely erased, with all final distributions favoring open structures, which the authors call consistent with single molecule FRET. No open or closed populations or other numbers reported in the text. Preprint
reference: Otten, 2026, bioRxiv preprint, no volume or page, 10.64898/2026.03.24.714034

system: Lysine, arginine and ornithine binding protein (LAOBP) with modeled Cu(II) NTA spin labels on I56H/K60H/D144H/S148H, ligand removed closed state (PDB 1LST) to open state (PDB 2LAO)
protocol: WE with MAB (6 bins per dimension), 2D coordinate (Cu to Cu distance and domain opening angle), τ 50 ps, 4 walkers per bin, WESTPA 2.0, then 15 μs of standard MD seeded from WE end states
outcome: 381 continuous closed to open pathways, open state Cu to Cu distances bimodal as in Q band DEER (peaks 3.5 and 4.6 nm). No rate constant, left for future work

system: Trp cage synthetic MD (SynMD, 10,500 state MSM from 208 µs atomistic MD, kinetic Monte Carlo)
lab: Zuckerman, Aristoff, Simpson and Webber (OHSU, Colorado State, Drexel, UC San Diego)
protocol: RiteWeight (randomized iterative trajectory reweighting, 10 or 1,000 random clusters per iteration) on 10,000 short segments started far from equilibrium, no WE resampling
outcome: RiteWeight recovered the exactly computable equilibrium distribution from strongly misdistributed data (error values only in figures, not verified)
reference: Kania 2026, Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 123, e2529246123, doi 10.1073/pnas.2529246123

system: Trp cage atomistic, segments from the 208 µs DESRES explicit solvent trajectory
lab: Zuckerman, Aristoff, Simpson and Webber (OHSU, Colorado State, Drexel, UC San Diego)
protocol: RiteWeight with equilibrium and source sink (NESS) boundary conditions, lag 0.2 to 100 ns, PyEMMA MSM comparison, no WE resampling
outcome: RiteWeight recovered the reference folding MFPT and net fluxes even at lag 1 ns or less, where MSMs underestimated the MFPT by an order of magnitude or more (MFPT value only in figures, not verified)
reference: Kania 2026, Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 123, e2529246123, doi 10.1073/pnas.2529246123

system: Trp cage (PDB 2JOF) folding and unfolding, synthetic MD (10,500 state SynMD model of the DESRES trajectory)
lab: Zuckerman, Aristoff, Simpson, Webber and OpenEye (OHSU, Colorado State, Drexel, UC San Diego, Cadence)
protocol: WE with variance optimized bins (equal πv in the discrepancy h) learned from an haMSM on 20 unoptimized runs, 20 walkers per bin, WESTPA 2.0 with a synMD module, compared with exact microstate and exact coarse grained bins
outcome: Optimized bins reduced run to run flux variance against RMSD bins for both directions, reference MFPTs from the SynMD matrix 2.04 µs (unfolding) and 9.03 µs (folding)

system: NTL9 (PDB 2HBB) folding, AMBER ff14SB with GB implicit solvent at γ 5 per ps and γ 80 per ps
lab: Zuckerman, Aristoff, Simpson, Webber and OpenEye (OHSU, Colorado State, Drexel, UC San Diego, Cadence)
protocol: WE with haMSM learned optimized bins (stratified clustering within RMSD bins, VAMP features), τ 100 ps, WESTPA 2.0 with AMBER16 on GPUs
outcome: High friction, all 10 optimized runs folded with fluxes spanning 12 orders of magnitude against 14 of 20 unoptimized runs spanning 35 orders, low friction optimization not clearly better (2 or 3 of 5 optimized runs folded against 4 of 5)

system: Trp cage, downsampled trajectory data from the RiteWeight study
protocol: Regularized (smoothed) RiteWeight interpolating raw and cluster average weights, no WE resampling
outcome: Smoothing stabilized convergence and improved stationary density estimates on small data sets at the cost of a small tunable bias (numbers not verified, abstract only). Preprint

system: Benzylhydantoin transporter Mhp1 (Microbacterium liquefaciens), outward open (PDB 2JLN) to inward open (PDB 2X79) transition, coarse grained double Go model
protocol: WE path sampling on four progress coordinates (DRMSD and three gate distances), τ 20 ps, Langevin dynamics on GPU OpenMM through PyOpenMM, custom WE package
outcome: Outward to inward rate 23.9 ± 1.7 per ms from two WE runs (model value, not compared to experiment), 68 percent of transitions follow strict alternating access at the first gate analysis line

system: Rhodobacter sphaeroides TSPO A139T (PDB 4UC1) with PK 11195 in a lipid bilayer
protocol: REVO (48 walkers, 3 runs per docked pose), OpenMM 7.1.1, CHARMM36 and CGenFF, plus MSMs
outcome: PK 11195 exits into the membrane between transmembrane helices rather than into solvent, 2285 exit events in over 40 μs total, MFPT 28 min and 260 min for two poses versus experimental residence time 34 min (human TSPO)

system: Tacrine permeation through a neat POPC bilayer
protocol: WE with MAB against fixed bins, WESTPA 2.0
outcome: MAB gave the first tacrine flux at about 5 ns against about 7 ns with fixed bins, and a flux 2 orders of magnitude higher for the length of the test. No permeability value reported here

system: Butanol permeation through a neat POPC bilayer
protocol: WE through the WESTPA 2.0 Python API on OpenEye Orion (AWS g4dn instances), OpenMM 7.5
outcome: Scaling demonstration, per iteration use reached thousands of GPUs within a few hours. No kinetic value reported

system: Tacrine permeation through a POPC bilayer (50 lipids per leaflet), TIP3P water, OpenFF Parsley and LIPID17
protocol: Steady state WE on the membrane normal z, τ 100 ps, four protocols (fixed bins or MAB with 30 bins, with or without WESS reweighting), WESTPA in the OpenEye Orion Permeability Floe with OpenMM 7.5 on AWS GPUs
outcome: log P_m −4.27 ± 0.24 (cm/s) with MAB plus WESS against MDCK LE −4.64 and PAMPA about −5.0, MFPT 4.6 ms from 8.1 μs of WE. MAB plus WESS cut the needed simulation time about threefold

system: (R) zacopride permeation through a POPC bilayer
protocol: MAB plus WESS WE protocol as for tacrine, WESTPA in Orion with OpenMM 7.5
outcome: log P_m −6.35 ± 0.22 (cm/s) against MDCK LE −5.23, MFPT 559.2 ms from 6.0 μs of WE

system: Sotalol permeation through a POPC bilayer
protocol: MAB plus WESS WE protocol as for tacrine, WESTPA in Orion with OpenMM 7.5
outcome: log P_m −5.32 ± 0.22 (cm/s) against MDCK LE −6.02 and PAMPA −5.58 or −6.74, MFPT 52.1 ms from 6.3 μs of WE

system: 1 butanol permeation across a double POPC bilayer, LIPID17
protocol: Tutorial 7.6, MAB with recursive outer bins and the HDF5 trajectory framework, WESTPA 2.0 with OpenMM
outcome: Teaching example, no permeability value verified
reference: Bogetti, 2023, Living J Comput Mol Sci, 5, 1655, 10.33011/livecoms.5.1.1655

system: HIV 1 TAR RNA (PDB 1ANR)
protocol: WExplore with Euler angle order parameters, CHARMM via OpenMM 5.0, CHARMM36
outcome: 652.8 ns of WExplore (about 8% of an 8.2 μs Anton run) sampled interhelical states the Anton run missed, with better a priori agreement with experimental NMR RDCs

system: Alanine dipeptide in implicit solvent, multiple reaction channels at two temperatures
protocol: WE path sampling of the full transition path ensemble, compared with transition path sampling on 2D model potentials
outcome: Fractional importance of each channel quantified including at 300 K where brute force is prohibitive (channel fractions not verified, abstract only). Preprint, no journal version found

system: Toy models only, Brownian particle in a 1D double well with colored noise, myopic self avoiding walk, 2D double well with two pathways
protocol: WE as path space resampling, static, randomly fluctuating (50 to 100) and adaptive Voronoi bins, in house code
outcome: Self avoiding walk success fraction (10.865 ± 0.015) percent by WE against (10.854 ± 0.004) percent brute force, adaptive Voronoi bins find the target after about 200τ

system: Alanine dipeptide, C7eq to C7ax isomerization, CHARMM19 with ACE implicit solvent
protocol: Steady state WE with recycling and enhanced WE (bin to bin rate matrix reweighting, the WESS idea), 30° × 30° dihedral bins, 20 walkers per bin, τ 100 fs, Langevin dynamics in CHARMM
outcome: Enhanced WE reached steady state flux in 150 ns total simulation against about 5 µs brute force at 300 K (60 ns against 70 ns at 500 K), first transitions after 10 ns against a brute force MFPT of 5 µs

system: K+ and 18 crown 6 ether (with methane and methane, Na+ and Cl−, methane and benzene, values not verified)
protocol: WE, explicit solvent MD
outcome: Efficiency gain over brute force at least 300 fold for the association rate constant and 1100 fold for the transition path time distribution

system: Alanine dipeptide, transitions between two stable states in both directions, atomistic model
protocol: Steady state WE path sampling (Bhatt 2010 protocol), error bars from eight independent simulations at 500 K
outcome: Fractions of four pathway types equal in forward and reverse steady states within error although rates differ by almost two orders of magnitude, 1.5 per ns A to B against 123 per ns B to A
reference: Bhatt 2011, J Chem Theory Comput 7, 2520, doi 10.1021/ct200086k

system: Alanine tetrapeptide (Ala4), AMBER ff99SB with GB implicit solvent (igb 1)
protocol: Equilibrium WE with α/β history labels and the non Markovian labeled rate matrix, 10 × 10 bins on dihedral distance and helix RMSD, τ 5 ps, AMBER 11 Langevin dynamics (WE driver not named)
outcome: Populations and MFPTs for two state pairs from five WE runs of 3.0 µs each agreed with 95 percent intervals of a 3.0 µs brute force run, each ns of molecular time cost about 200 ns of total WE simulation (MFPT values only in figures, not verified)
reference: Suárez 2014, J Chem Theory Comput 10, 2658, doi 10.1021/ct401065r

system: Methane pair association and dissociation in TIP3P water (about 900 waters), GROMOS 45a3
protocol: Equilibrium WE on the methane separation (1 Å bins), τ 0.5 ps, GROMACS 4.5, direct, labeled non Markovian and Markov matrix estimators
outcome: Direct and non Markovian matrix MFPTs agreed with a 0.4 µs brute force interval for a range of state boundaries, while the plain Markov matrix estimate fell outside it (MFPT values only in figures, not verified)
reference: Suárez 2014, J Chem Theory Comput 10, 2658, doi 10.1021/ct401065r

system: Bistable dimer in a dense WCA fluid (216 particles)
protocol: WE with fixed bins, WESTPA with OpenMM 6.1
outcome: Extension distribution matches a 2.5 × 10⁸ step brute force run, rates within brute force 95% intervals (figures only)

system: Alanine tetrapeptide (Ala4), AMBER ff99SB with GB implicit solvent (igb 1)
protocol: WE with WESTPA (2D bins, at most 5 walkers per bin, τ 5 ps, AMBER 11) followed by non Markovian labeled matrix FPT distribution analysis
outcome: Non Markovian FPT distribution agreed with the interval from about 3 µs of MD with 1038 events (values only in figures, not verified)

system: Methane pair association in SPC/E water, GROMOS 45a3
protocol: WE with WESTPA (10 bins, τ 0.5 ps, GROMACS 4.6.3) and non Markovian FPT distribution analysis
outcome: Non Markovian FPT distribution agreed with the interval from 1.0 µs of MD with about 1200 events, also recovered from a short MD trajectory with 30 events (values only in figures, not verified)

system: Na+/Cl− ion pair association in SPC/E water
protocol: WE with WESTPA (21 bins, τ 5 ps, GROMACS 4.6.3) and non Markovian FPT distribution analysis
outcome: Non Markovian FPT distribution agreed with the interval from 1.0 µs of MD with about 1600 events (values only in figures, not verified)

system: Cucurbit[8]uril with quinine (SAMPL6 CB8 G3)
protocol: REVO (first use, named here Reweighting of Ensembles by Variance Optimization), OpenMM 7.1.1
outcome: k_off 0.012 s⁻¹ and k_on 4.7 × 10⁸ M⁻¹ s⁻¹, ΔG from rate ratio −16.0 kcal/mol versus alchemical reference −10.90 and experimental −6.45 kcal/mol

system: Octa acid with 5 hexenoic acid (SAMPL6 OA G3)
protocol: REVO, OpenMM 7.1.1
outcome: k_off 160 s⁻¹ and k_on 1.2 × 10⁸ M⁻¹ s⁻¹, ΔG −9.5 kcal/mol versus reference −6.70 and experimental −5.18 kcal/mol

system: Octa acid with 4 methyl pentanoic acid (SAMPL6 OA G6)
protocol: REVO, OpenMM 7.1.1
outcome: k_off 0.48 s⁻¹ and k_on 2.8 × 10⁸ M⁻¹ s⁻¹, ΔG −12.1 kcal/mol versus reference −7.18 and experimental −4.97 kcal/mol

system: Na+ and Cl− association in water (basic tutorial)
protocol: Steady state WE in WESTPA, OpenMM 7.3
outcome: Tutorial showing flux based rate estimation from WE, no rate value reported in text (not verified)
reference: Bogetti 2019, Living J Comput Mol Sci 1, 10607, 10.33011/livecoms.1.2.10607

system: K+/18 crown 6 ether dissociation (advanced tutorial 2)
protocol: WExplore plugin for WESTPA (Dickson lab), GROMACS 2016.2
outcome: Tutorial on hierarchical Voronoi WE with a user defined distance metric, 50 iterations, no rate reported in text (not verified)
reference: Bogetti 2019, Living J Comput Mol Sci 1, 10607, 10.33011/livecoms.1.2.10607

system: Toy model only, 1D overdamped Langevin particle (β 5) on a rugged two superbasin potential, MFPT estimation
protocol: Steady state WE with variance optimized allocation and binning from a microbin Markov estimate of the discrepancy h (Algorithms 5.1 and 5.2), in house code
outcome: Order of magnitude lower standard deviation of the steady state flux (MFPT) than direct Monte Carlo with only M = 4 bins, further reduction with 16 bins

system: Octa acid with 4 methyl pentanoic acid (SAMPL6 OA G6)
protocol: REVO unbinding and rebinding ensembles at three Langevin friction coefficients, OpenMM 7.2.1, GAFF
outcome: Derived correction terms cut the rate ratio free energy error versus the alchemical benchmark from 3.4 to 0.76 kcal/mol, corrected ΔG −8.13 kcal/mol at γ = 1 ps⁻¹ versus computed −7.0 and experimental −4.97 kcal/mol, k_off 16.4 s⁻¹

system: Lennard Jones atom pairs with well depths 2 to 20 kcal/mol (sole system)
protocol: WE nonequilibrium Jarzynski pulling with REVO, also importance resampling and diffusion Monte Carlo, wepy with OpenMM 7.4.0
outcome: At ε = 20 kcal/mol REVO final free energy RMSE 0.49 kJ/mol, about half of straightforward pulling (0.78 kJ/mol), and REVO significantly better than straightforward after 400 trajectories at ε = 10 kcal/mol

system: Cucurbit[8]uril with quinine (SAMPL6 CB8 G3)
lab: Chodera, Mobley, Shirts, Gilson, Dickson and others (SAMPL6 SAMPLing)
protocol: OpenMM/REVO entry, REVO in wepy with OpenMM, compared with alchemical and PMF methods
outcome: REVO ΔG −16.0 ± 1.0 kcal/mol, systematically more negative than the other methods by about 5 to 6 kcal/mol, and the rate ratio route was about an order of magnitude less efficient than direct free energy methods

system: Octa acid with 5 hexenoic acid (SAMPL6 OA G3)
lab: Chodera, Mobley, Shirts, Gilson, Dickson and others (SAMPL6 SAMPLing)
protocol: OpenMM/REVO entry, REVO in wepy with OpenMM
outcome: REVO ΔG −11.0 ± 2.0 kcal/mol, the only entry whose five replicates were not within 0.1 to 0.4 kcal/mol, ligand ranking agreed with the other methods

system: Octa acid with 4 methyl pentanoic acid (SAMPL6 OA G6)
lab: Chodera, Mobley, Shirts, Gilson, Dickson and others (SAMPL6 SAMPLing)
protocol: OpenMM/REVO entry, REVO in wepy with OpenMM
outcome: REVO ΔG −12.0 ± 1.0 kcal/mol, systematically more negative than the alchemical entries (for example AMBER/APR −6.8 ± 0.1 kcal/mol)

system: Na+ and Cl− ion pair association, explicit TIP3P water
protocol: RED scheme against the original flux estimate, five steady state WE runs (τ 2 ps, 0.2 μs each), WESTPA with AMBER18
outcome: No ramp up in flux, so RED gave little efficiency gain over the original estimate, both compared with ten 1 μs standard MD runs. Rate values in Table S1, not verified

system: Na+ and Cl− ion pair association, explicit TIP3P water
protocol: WE with MAB against manual fixed bins (28 bins), RED rate estimate, WESTPA with AMBER18
outcome: k_on (3.9 ± 0.3) × 10^10 M−1 s−1 with MAB and (4.1 ± 0.4) × 10^10 with manual bins against (3.9 ± 0.3) × 10^10 from five 1 μs standard MD runs. Efficiency S_k 5.1 (MAB) and 3.1 (manual), a 1.6 fold gain, 2498 against 1226 pathways

system: Na+ and Cl− ion pair association, explicit water
protocol: Three WE runs with the new per iteration HDF5 trajectory storage, WESTPA 2.0 with OpenMM 7.5
outcome: 27% average reduction in trajectory file size against WESTPA 1.0, with no significant runtime cost. Storage test only, no rate reported

system: Octa acid with 5 hexenoic acid (SAMPL6 OA G3)
protocol: Reanalysis of REVO unbinding trajectories (wepy) from Dixon 2018 and Hall 2020
outcome: Low Na+ density above the binding pocket along transition paths is associated with up to 10⁶ fold higher unbinding path probabilities

system: Octa acid with 4 methyl pentanoic acid (SAMPL6 OA G6)
protocol: Reanalysis of REVO unbinding trajectories (wepy) from Dixon 2018 and Hall 2020
outcome: Low Na+ density above the binding pocket along transition paths is associated with up to 10⁶ fold higher unbinding path probabilities

system: Alanine dipeptide in gas phase
protocol: M WEM plugin, WESTPA 2.0 with NAMD 2.14
outcome: MFPT about 1.2 ns against about 1.6 ns from conventional MD (read from a figure)
reference: Bogetti 2023, Living J Comput Mol Sci 5, 1655, 10.33011/livecoms.5.1.1655

system: Na+ and Cl− ion pair association, explicit water
protocol: Tutorials 7.1 (basic fixed bins) and 7.5 (binless resampler grouping walkers by k means), WESTPA 2.0
outcome: Teaching example, no new benchmark number reported
reference: Bogetti, 2023, Living J Comput Mol Sci, 5, 1655, 10.33011/livecoms.5.1.1655

system: Alanine dipeptide conformational change, gas phase
protocol: Tutorial 7.9, Markovian WE milestoning (M WEM) with WESTPA 2.0 and NAMD 2.14 (Colvars)
outcome: Teaching example, free energy landscape and transition kinetics demonstrated, no number verified
reference: Bogetti, 2023, Living J Comput Mol Sci, 5, 1655, 10.33011/livecoms.5.1.1655

system: Alanine dipeptide C7eq to C7ax transition, GB implicit solvent, ff14SBonlysc
protocol: Five WE runs with fixed bins on ψ (20° spacing) and a φ/ψ coordinate, τ 100 ps, WESTPA, pathways clustered with LPATH
outcome: 80 pathways from 14.6 μs of WE against 30 from 14.6 μs of standard MD. Two pathway classes, upper route 87.5% and lower route 12.5%

system: Toy model only, 2D Smoluchowski particle (β 30) in a model potential, MFPT estimation
lab: Zuckerman, Aristoff, Simpson and Webber (OHSU, Colorado State, Drexel, Caltech)
protocol: Steady state WE with MFPT bins in the flux discrepancy h and allocation proportional to πv, microbin estimates on a 49 × 49 Voronoi grid, WeightedEnsemble.jl, τ 0.01
outcome: MFPT binning gave 3 to 5 orders of magnitude lower normalized variance than radial bins and about 2.5 orders below brute force with 40 bins, radial bins were worse than brute force

system: β cyclodextrin with promazine (SAMPL9 β CD PMZ)
protocol: Cutoff REVO (cloning blocked in quasi unbound states, introduced here) versus standard REVO, wepy with OpenMM
outcome: Prospective ΔG −5.00 ± 0.66 kcal/mol with cutoff REVO (−5.05 with REVO) versus experimental −4.97 kcal/mol as printed in Table 4

system: Octa acid with 4 methyl pentanoic acid (SAMPL6 OA G6)
protocol: Cutoff REVO versus standard REVO, wepy with OpenMM
outcome: ΔG −5.21 kcal/mol with cutoff REVO (−6.55 with REVO) versus computational reference −7.18 and experimental −4.97 kcal/mol

system: Octa acid with 5 hexenoic acid (SAMPL6 OA G3)
protocol: Cutoff REVO versus standard REVO, wepy with OpenMM
outcome: ΔG −6.49 kcal/mol with cutoff REVO (−7.69 with REVO) versus computational reference −6.71 and experimental −5.18 kcal/mol

system: Cucurbit[8]uril with quinine (SAMPL6 CB8 G3)
protocol: Cutoff REVO versus standard REVO, wepy with OpenMM
outcome: ΔG −11.17 ± 0.13 kcal/mol with cutoff REVO (−11.35 ± 1.01 with REVO) versus computational reference −10.80 and experimental −6.45 kcal/mol

system: Alanine dipeptide C7eq to C7ax transition, GB implicit solvent, ff14SBonlysc
protocol: Same five WE run dataset as LPATH (2D φ/ψ coordinate, τ 100 ps, WESTPA 2.0 with Amber 22, 21 h on 8 CPU cores per run), pathways clustered with SHINE in MDANCE
